chunks: Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, all from Ibn Abi Umayr from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said:
The charity (Zakat) is not due upon the fed ones, nor upon the nourisher, and the nourisher is that which feeds two, nor upon a milking sheep, nor upon the stallion of the sheep.

key_terms.الرُّبَّى: A male sheep that feeds two females
key_terms.الْأَكِيلَة: Sheep kept for meat (not for breeding or milk)
key_terms.شَاةِ لَبَنٍ: A sheep kept for its milk
key_terms.فَحْلِ الْغَنَمِ: The breeding ram of the sheep

ai.seo_question: What types of sheep are exempt from paying Zakat in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates specific exemptions from Zakat for sheep, reflecting the Shia juristic distinction between livestock kept for subsistence (such as meat, milk, or breeding) versus those held as commercial wealth. By excluding the 'Akilah' and 'Rubba', the Imam emphasizes that Zakat is primarily levied on surplus or trade-oriented assets, a nuance that distinguishes Shia fiqh from some other schools regarding the definition of nisab-eligible livestock.
